title: MeshStream congestion validator for mixed-tenant continuous batching
creator: Avery Thompson
description:
Goal: Build a deterministic, repeatable validator (MeshStream) that stresses continuous batching + queueing interactions under mixed-tenant traffic and surfaces tokens/sec and p95 regressions automatically.

Motivation and hypothesis:
- Continuous batching is a major cost saver, but queueing interactions across heterogeneous session profiles can amplify tail latency unpredictably. We believe that specific mixes (long-token, short-token, high-arrival bursts) create persistent queue-head creation that reduces effective batching and increases p95.
- Current harnesses focus on single-profile probes or burst-only scenarios. MeshStream will synthesize steady-state multiplexed tenants with controlled burstiness to reveal steady-state congestion modes that prior probes miss.

Design summary (high level):
1) Traffic model: N tenant classes with configurable proportions: short-chat (40%, 8-32 tokens), long-generation (20%, 512-2048 tokens), embedding-heavy (20%, 1-4 tokens but high concurrency), interactive-microbursts (20%, 10-100 tokens with Poisson bursts). Session stickiness and warm KV-cache probabilities are configurable per-class.
2) Arrival shaping: mixture of Poisson and Weibull interarrival generators to simulate both memoryless and bursty arrival patterns. We will support synthetic traces derived from production sampling (anonymized) and a canonical synthetic family for reproducibility.
3) Serving topology: multi-model/multi-queue topology to emulate tenant colocation and priority hierarchies. Batching settings and kernel-opt variants (fp16, int8/qtz) will be toggled.
4) Metrics and detection: tokens/sec (aggregate and per-tenant), p50/p95/p99 per route, batch formation latency distribution, batch size histogram, queue depth over time, KV cache hit ratio, and quantile drift. Regression detection uses a rolling baseline with two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov and an exponentially-weighted moving average on p95; alerts when p95 increases by >=20% vs baseline for 10+ minutes and tokens/sec drops >=15%.
5) Automation & outputs: run matrix generator produces permutation sets (workload mix x arrival model x cache warm fraction x batch settings). Results are stored as per-run artifacts (JSON + CSV + Grafana snapshots) and summarized in a single-line verdict (PASS/WARN/FAIL) with a textual explanation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can run reproducible 1-hour steady-state experiments that reproduce within 5% for tokens/sec and within 10% for p95 across 3 repeated runs of the same configuration.
- Regression detector triggers on an injected slow-path (artificial kernel delay) and annotates which metric (batch size drop / queue depth increase / kv miss change) most strongly correlates.
- Reports include an automated root-cause candidate list and links to relevant flamegraphs / GPU utilization traces and the exact seed + configuration needed to reproduce.

Implementation tasks (initial MVP):
- Create traffic-generator binary with class-based workload templates and seeding (ENG-224999-1).
- Integrate with existing runner harness and extend snapshot schema to include batch formation timing and batch composition (ENG-224999-2).
- Implement rolling-baseline detector and dashboard prototype with alert rules (ENG-224999-3).
- Run a 12-config matrix across dedicated test fleet (4 cards) and collect baseline results (ENG-224999-4).

Infra and risk notes:
- Requires controlled test nodes isolated from other CI traffic to avoid noise; coordinate with infra to reserve nodes (request documented in comments).
- Synthetic traces derived from production must be scrubbed: will follow privacy checklist (no identifiers, fixed seed transformations).
- False positives are a risk; detection thresholds will be tuned after initial baseline runs.

Artifacts and links:
- Traffic templates and canonical config: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/MeshStream+Templates
- Runner PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1256
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/meshstream/meshstream-congestion
